title: Robust cavity metrology beyond the limits of Pound-Drever-Hall
authors: Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Yanqin Huang, Nathan Schine, Kevin C. Cox, Alicia J. Kollár
abstract: Precise measurement of the resonance frequencies of microwave and optical cavities is a foundational capability across quantum technologies. One of the highest-performance methods currently available is Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) spectroscopy, which relies on a three-tone interrogation and eliminates sensitivity to path-length fluctuations. However, PDH is known to suffer from systematic offsets due to residual amplitude modulation and demodulation-phase errors. Here we leverage an optimal linear combination of the phases of the three interrogation tones to implement a method for robust cavity metrology which eliminates significant systematic-error sensitivities of PDH. We experimentally demonstrate robust cavity measurements in both the optical and microwave frequency regime, showing insensitivity to sideband imbalance and demodulation phase, as well as demonstrating single-shot readout of a cavity-coupled superconducting qubit.
summary: This paper introduces a robust metrology technique, the scissors observable ($S_Q$), designed to overcome systematic errors inherent in standard Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) spectroscopy. By analyzing the optimal linear combination of three interrogation tones, the authors demonstrate that $S_Q$ maintains high measurement fidelity in both optical and superconducting qubit readout regimes, even when subjected to significant technical phase and amplitude imbalances.
main_problem: The paper addresses the systematic limitations of Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) spectroscopy in high-precision cavity metrology, specifically due to residual amplitude modulation and demodulation-phase errors.
main_result: A novel observable, the scissors phase ($S_Q$), was developed and experimentally demonstrated to be robust against common-mode and differential-mode phase errors, outperforming conventional PDH methods in both optical and microwave regimes.
method: The authors propose and test an optimal linear combination of the phases of three interrogation tones, leading to the $S_Q$ observable, which is measured using a three-frequency heterodyne setup.
model_or_system: The work utilizes microwave and optical cavities, applying the metrology techniques to stabilize optical frequencies and read out the state of superconducting qubits.
key_observables: Conventional PDH signal ($\epsilon_Q$), ideal scissors phase ($\Sigma$), and the experimentally efficient scissors observable ($S_Q$).
important_parameters: Sideband imbalance ($\Delta_{amp}$), demodulation phase error ($ eta$), and cavity linewidth ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The superior robustness of $S_Q$ is achieved by using a three-frequency heterodyne setup, which is computationally more complex than standard PDH.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three-tone interrogation scheme and compare the zero-crossing shifts of $\epsilon_Q$ and $S_Q$ under induced hardware imperfections (imbalance, phase offsets). Other figures show single-shot IQ distributions for qubit readout.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the limitations of PDH, then derives the robust scissors phase observable ($\Sigma$), and finally proposes the computationally simpler, yet equally robust, $S_Q$ observable. The methodology is validated through extensive optical and microwave experiments comparing the performance of $\epsilon_Q$, $\Sigma$, and $S_Q$ under controlled error injection.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the practical limitations of high-precision quantum measurement techniques, providing a robust diagnostic tool ($S_Q$) essential for advancing quantum sensing and quantum information processing platforms.
